meta.title: Operation of HPTLC System in Pharmaceutical Analysis Laboratory

sections.purpose: To perform High Performance Thin Layer Chromatography for qualitative identification, semi-quantitative estimation, and purity assessment of pharmaceutical substances and herbal drug extracts using automated sample application and densitometric scanning.
sections.scope: Applicable to Pharmaceutical Analysis laboratory for drug identity testing, herbal fingerprinting, stability studies, and identification of related substances as per IP/BP/USP methods.
procedure: Prepare the HPTLC silica gel 60 F254 plates (10 × 10 cm or 20 × 10 cm, aluminium-backed) by activation in an oven at 110°C for 10 minutes immediately before use.
Allow the activated plates to cool in a desiccator before use.
Program the automatic sample applicator (CAMAG Linomat or ATS) with: application volume, band width (5–10 mm), track spacing, and start position.
Prepare sample and standard solutions at the specified concentrations in appropriate solvents.
Load the syringe of the applicator with sample/standard; apply as bands at defined positions on the plate.
Saturate the twin-trough developing chamber with the mobile phase for 20 minutes with a filter paper lining.
Place the plate in the chamber — liquid level must be 5 mm below the application bands.
Develop to the specified migration distance (typically 80 mm from the application point).
Remove plate immediately when the solvent front reaches the mark; mark the solvent front in pencil.
Dry the plate in a current of warm air or in the drying oven at 60°C for 5 minutes.
Visualize under UV 254 nm (fluorescence quenching) and 366 nm (fluorescence) using the CAMAG UV cabinet.
Document UV images using the densitometer or UV cabinet camera.
Apply derivatization reagent (if required): spray in fume hood; heat per method.
Scan the plate using the densitometer at specified wavelengths; record peak areas and Rf values.
Calculate purity or content using peak area ratios: Sample area / Standard area × Standard concentration.
Document all parameters, images, and numerical results in the analytical register.
precautions: Wear UV-protective goggles when examining plates under UV light — short-wave UV (254 nm) causes severe eye damage.
Handle spray reagents (H₂SO₄, vanillin, anisaldehyde) in a fume hood; wear acid-resistant gloves.
Activate HPTLC plates immediately before use — moisture uptake from air reduces efficiency.
Ensure uniform application of sample bands — uneven bands cause asymmetric peaks and quantification errors.
Chamber saturation is critical — unsaturated chambers give reproducibility failures.
Mark the solvent front immediately on plate removal — it moves rapidly after removal.
Do not touch the plate surface in the chromatographic region — fingerprints cause background fluorescence.
